title: AgentDesktop Runtime API agentdesktop.runtime/1 (draft, PR1 read-only surface)

notSent.description: not_performed: true only when the Runtime (or the client, before sending) can prove this request sent no input and made no write with an outside effect, whether or not it reached the Runtime. Never true for a partial send, a timeout, a lost connection, a missing receipt or an unknown outcome. Not a licence to retry: a retry is judged again by authorization, Run state, stops, policy and the request ledger.

details.description: Code-specific facts. writeOutcome "completed" (#203): a write the service did before the caller lost its access (client_revoked, grant_missing, grant_expired); its answer is withheld and notSent is false. recovery then says how to find the outcome: "look_up_same_request_id" (grant_expired, grant_missing: the client keeps its id, so the same requestId reads it; a new one would write again) or "check_outcome_do_not_resubmit" (client_revoked: pairing again gives a new client id the request ledger does not know).

includeOffscreen.description: also minimized, hidden and other-Space windows; default on-screen only

source.description: commit the product was built from, or "unknown" outside a bundled build

gui.description: what the GUI execution backend supports, as the AI service reports it (ai-gui/v1 runtime_capabilities_result); absent while that service is not running

kind.description: virtual: a display the Runtime created and destroys; physical: one of the user's displays, attached; absent means virtual

startedAt.description: process start time; pid plus start time names one launch

title.description: null when the OS withholds titles (no Screen Recording grant)

physical.description: attach one of the user's own displays instead of creating a virtual one: nothing is created, window.bind needs windowId and never moves the window, app.launch is refused, desktop.destroy only drops the record; with physical, width and height are refused (the display's size applies)

displayId.description: a physical display's ID; default the main display

elements.description: default true; needs a bound window

windowGrantId.description: the caller's window grant this binding was made under; absent for the owner's bindings and an app's own launched windows

quitApps.description: apps launched onto the Desktop that were asked to quit

transient.description: true: kept only briefly (no persist permission for the window); gone at expiresAt or when the window grant ends

coverage.description: what this observation could see: the element read may be partial (truncated walk) or unavailable (deadline passed, a read of the Desktop still running) while the screenshot is complete

clientId.description: the principal that made the request

desktopId.description: the Desktop the request named (absent for records older than A5 or naming none)

Action.description: hover rests the pointer on the target; press is an accessibility press of one element (elementRef only), never an event click; drag goes from target to `to`. hover and drag are refused with unsupported_backend where the backend cannot do them in the background without side effects (macOS today: hover would be a middle click, drag would take the real pointer and the foreground), never done otherwise instead

businessResult.description: delivery is not effect; a later observation or the caller establishes the effect

reason.description: why the action was not delivered, failed or has an unknown outcome; absent when delivered

lifetime.description: accepted only to refuse escalation explicitly

Principal.description: who the Runtime holds this connection to be (A4): from the credential shown in runtime.handshake, never from params

codeIdentityLevel.description: how far the Runtime can tell this connection's program from other processes of the user (A4 S2)

lifetime.description: accepted only to refuse escalation explicitly

cursor.description: resume with events.subscribe after=cursor: the sequence for a Run stream, the global cursor otherwise

transient.description: true: kept only briefly (no persist permission for the window); gone at expiresAt or when the window grant ends

PlatformRunEvent.description: the events the Runtime writes on every Run; RunEvent types with the prefix run., action. or stop. are these. The prefix unit. is the GUI unit's own (UnitRunEvent, A6); other prefixes are reserved.

RunUnit.description: present only on kind unit: the GUI unit's own facts, beside the Run's phase/outcome/quiescence

UnitVerification.description: every predicate must hold on a fresh observation; each is a service.schema.json GuiVerification

agentName.description: one line of printable text, shown to the user as self-reported (no control, line-separator or bidi characters)

publisher.description: one line of printable text, shown to the user as self-reported (no control, line-separator or bidi characters)

WindowGrantWindow.description: the window a grant covers: window ID together with the process launch (pid + start time) and its app; a window ID alone is never an identity

endedReason.description: why it no longer holds: window_closed, process_changed, app_changed, window_grant_revoked, client_revoked, grant_revoked, app_removed, desktop_removed, desktop_destroyed

windowId.description: omitted: the app's frontmost window where the Desktop can bind it; the user confirms the window shown

includeEnded.description: also revoked and ended grants; default active only

CodeIdentity.description: what the Runtime read from the socket peer's kernel audit token (A4 S2), never from anything the client sends. verified: team-signed, hardened runtime, bound by its designated requirement; shared_interpreter: as verified but an interpreter whose every script shares it; same_user: nothing verifiable, only a process of this user; in_process: the host itself

requirement.description: the designated requirement every later connection of this client must satisfy

name.description: the display's product name as the system reports it, or a neutral name when it reports none

origin.description: as the Runtime proved it: physical (built in, or an external display a hardware framebuffer vouches for), virtual (a display some process created), unconfirmed (not provably either; refused)

originDetail.description: why it is virtual or unconfirmed

attachable.description: origin physical and not attached yet

desktopId.description: the physical Desktop already attached to it, if any

HubDisplay.description: one of the user's active displays, for the owner to open to a paired client (owner-display-attach.md)

displayId.description: a display hub.displays.list reports as physical

clientId.description: the paired client whose grant gains the Desktop

name.description: the Desktop's name when it is created now; ignored for a display already attached

grant.description: the client's grant as it is now, naming the Desktop

created.description: false when the display was already attached and that Desktop was reused

clientId.description: only this client loses the Desktop; omitted: every client does and the Desktop is destroyed

grants.description: the grants the Desktop was removed from, as they are now

DesktopControl.description: who controls the Desktop's input, derived from its lease, its admission and its last Run (docs/plan/03 §3.4); a paired client sees controllerRunId, clientId and clientName only for its own Run

state.description: running: a Run holds the lease; manual: the user's takeover Run holds it; stopping: the Run holding it stops; stopped: desktop.stop, global stop, or the last Run ended by a stop, until a new Run or desktop.handback; disconnected: the last Run lost its control connection; unknown: the last Run has an unknown action; creating and error are reserved

run.description: the Run that held the Desktop, as stopped: phase stopping and quiescence pending while an action of it is in flight

stopped.description: the agent's Run the takeover stopped, if one held the Desktop

elements.description: default true; needs a bound window

UnitRunEvent.description: the GUI unit's own events on a kind unit Run (A6, F40-03), beside the PlatformRunEvent types. data holds ids, enums, codes and numbers only: never a screenshot, typed text, a window title, a goal or parameter value, a model reply or a secret. Lifecycle (phase, outcome) stays in the run.* events.

attempts.description: model calls this inference made (a transient failure moved to the next candidate counts each); inferenceAttemptId names the last, and is absent when the calls failed with no receipt

kind.description: reobserve_after_empty_reply: a step's empty model reply (Kevin 2026-10-08). The others (X1-2): a stall took its one bounded recovery — a new observation of the bound target, verified; nothing sent is repeated. A further stall ends the Run with closingReason no_progress (repeated_action, no_progress) or loop_detected (state_loop).

reason.description: why an inconclusive verdict could not decide; absent otherwise

display.description: a virtual Desktop's display is destroyed; a physical one is the user's and kept

quit.description: processes destroy asks to quit: launched on this Desktop and still running

keep.description: processes with a window there that destroy leaves running

exited.description: the process is gone; false: asked to quit, not proof that it will

clientId.description: owner only: one caller's records; ignored for a paired client, which sees only its own
owner only: one caller's records; ignored for a paired client, which sees only its own

truncated.description: more records matched than one export holds (10000): narrow the filter
